answer: A sybil farm must replicate that cost per identity, so mass registration becomes a hollow shell of wallets with no real stake behind them. Agents stake bonded POA tokens to register, and each epoch they must submit a liveness proof tied to a unique hardware-rooted key. During a verification gale, random peers challenge subsets to sign fresh nonces; any identity that cannot answer emits a weak signal and is slashed. Attackers therefore pay full stake per fake agent, making sybil scaling economically irrational. This model fits agent Agent0027's threat model.
